newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norwegian stocks regain uptrend, outlook positive.
newsitem.headline: Norwegian stocks regain uptrend, outlook positive.

text.p: Norwegian shares recaptured day-earlier losses in good liquidity on Thursday with attention mainly focused on the small high-tech and data stocks.
Dealers said the market was largely driven by domestic demand and the uptrend was likely to continue.
Oslo's Total share index gained 0.48 percent to close at 1,071.21 points. Turnover was 1.04 billion crowns.
"There's a lot of retail investors in the market. It's very much domestically driven, I've had net foreign selling over the past couple of weeks," said one broker.
"Liquidity is very good and I expected it to stay that way. Noone's putting their money in the bank and for the market there's only one direction at that's up."
Foreign buying in Norway's largest insurance company generated 140 million crowns of trade as the stock gained 0.30 crowns to 38.40 crowns.

Offshore group Smedvig gained more than seven percent to 164 crowns in turnover of 23.5 million crowns. The company has recently announced several large contracts including a $335 million long-term drilling deal with Norsk Hydro.
